title: Refrigeration Systems Attacks Agentic AI Investigative Assessment
executiveAssessment: The strongest public evidence establishes that a large-scale cyber campaign affected commercial refrigeration systems in France beginning 11-12 October 2026 , followed by a wider EU wave on 1-2 November 2026 , and a separate but temporally related compromise of refrigeration control systems used by France's national blood service on 1-2 November 2026 . ENISA publicly confirmed incidents across multiple EU member states since 11 October 2026, and U.S. agencies publicly warned on 5 November 2026 that malicious actors are targeting industrial refrigeration and cold-chain monitoring systems globally. ENISA Joint Statement, 4 Nov 2026 ; U.S. Government Fact Sheet, 5 Nov 2026 CONFIRMED FACT French government cyber-crisis authorities stated that an attack on approximately 700 French retail sites modified defrost parameters to high temperatures, caused significant merchandise losses, and in at least 15 cases coincided with fires. That statement is the most authoritative public account of the October France incident. CERTFR-2026-CTI-009 CONFIRMED FACT ENISA stated that "several commercial refrigeration systems and similar devices" in a number of EU member states were impacted since 11 October 2026 , with a new wave on 1-2 November . ENISA Joint Statement, 4 Nov 2026 CONFIRMED FACT France's blood service (EFS) confirmed that a cyber incident affecting an external refrigeration provider altered temperature/defrost thresholds at three sites ; public reporting states alarms enabled intervention before blood products were compromised. This establishes a public-safety-relevant OT event, but not confirmed product loss. Recorded Future News / The Record, 4 Nov 2026 ; The Connexion, 4 Nov 2026 ASSESSMENT Public evidence supports the conclusion that these incidents primarily involved internet-accessible or remotely accessible refrigeration controllers / supervisory systems , insecure remote management, weak/default credentials, and/or known vulnerabilities in affected controller families. That assessment is strongly supported by the 5 November U.S. multi-agency fact sheet, the French warning scope naming affected product families, and multiple national follow-on advisories. Confidence: Moderate . U.S. Government Fact Sheet, 5 Nov 2026 ; ENISA ; Ireland NCSC advisory, 13 Nov 2026 ; Swiss NCSC/BACS advisory, 10 Nov 2026 ASSESSMENT The October French retail attack and the November EFS incident share sectoral and technical characteristics, but public evidence does not prove the same initial-access path or operator in both events. Relationship: Possible but not fully established . Confidence: Moderate . ASSESSMENT With respect to attribution, the public record is split by incident. For the 11-12 October 2026 France retail attack , a French interagency cyber-crisis document publicly attributes the operation to Iranian IRGC cyber elements, specifically Shahid Kaveh / Shahid Shoostari-linked offensive units. That is a high-authority government assessment for that incident. For the broader EU wave and the EFS incident , public attribution remains less complete and should not be generalized without additional evidence. Confidence: Moderate overall; higher for the October France event than for the full campaign . CERTFR-2026-CTI-009 UNRESOLVED Publicly available evidence is insufficient to determine whether the late-August 2026 U.S. military commissary refrigeration outages were technically linked to the EU incidents. Public reporting confirms an investigation and suspected cyber dimension, but not a verified causal chain, affected controller family, or relationship to the EU events. Nextgov/FCW, 29 Oct 2026 ; Stars and Stripes, 1 Sep 2026 Bottom line: The evidence supports a real, ongoing OT threat to refrigeration and cold-chain systems with demonstrated impacts in retail and blood-storage contexts, confirmed cross-border relevance in Europe, and enough concern for U.S. federal agencies to issue sector-wide defensive guidance. The evidence does not support merging all reported refrigeration failures into one confirmed campaign or attributing all incidents to a single actor.

sections.heading: KEY FINDINGS
sections.text: Finding: Large-scale France retail compromise occurred 11-12 Oct 2026 CONFIRMED FACT HIGH CONFIDENCE French interagency cyber-crisis authorities reported compromise of refrigeration controllers at about 700 retail sites, high-temperature defrost changes, major product losses, and at least 15 fires. sections.heading: AFFECTED SYSTEMS
sections.text: Confirmed affected organizations / sectors French large retail / food distribution sector : French government document names Casino, Leclerc, Coopérative U, Metro, Carrefour, and Intermarché among affected entities, with additional food-sector victims including small butcheries, a slaughterhouse, and cooperative food factories. CERTFR-2026-CTI-009 France's national blood service (EFS) : three sites affected via refrigeration-equipment provider. The Record ; The Connexion Multiple EU member states : ENISA confirms incidents in a number of EU member states; public secondary reporting references Belgium, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Sweden, Ireland, and others, but country-by-country confirmation is uneven in primary sources. ENISA U.S. military commissaries : confirmed refrigeration outages under investigation; not commercial-sector operations, but relevant U.S.-based refrigeration activity. Stars and Stripes ; Nextgov/FCW U.S. meat processing facility in Los Angeles area (historical comparison): DOJ says Nov 2024 attack spoiled meat and triggered ammonia leak. DOJ Confirmed / publicly named technologies Danfoss AK-SM / AK-SC families : repeatedly named in public advisories and incident reporting. Swiss advisory ; Ireland NCSC Copeland XWEB / Dixell XWEB : identified in later public warning scope and technical reporting. Ireland NCSC ; Copeland XWEB PRO bulletin (Feb 2026) Electronic temperature controllers / commercial refrigeration controllers : explicitly identified by U.S. government fact sheet. U.S. Government Fact Sheet Internet-exposed controller panels / web interfaces : directly cited as risk by U.S. and European guidance. U.S. Government Fact Sheet ; Swiss advisory OT / ICS components implicated by available evidence Controller panels and supervisory refrigeration controllers. U.S. Government Fact Sheet Cold-room monitoring and control systems. The Record Remote monitoring / remote management functions and internet-facing administration interfaces. U.S. Government Fact Sheet ; Swiss advisory UNRESOLVED Public reporting does not consistently disclose PLC, HMI, engineering workstation, VPN, or vendor-remote-support product names for each incident. Some of those layers may have been involved, but they are not publicly verified .

Collect national CERT advisories from all affected EU states to compare named products, mitigations, and any disclosed IOCs. Review vendor advisories from Danfoss, Copeland, Dixell, and Johnson Controls for remote-access architecture, fixed vulnerabilities, and end-of-life notices. sections.heading: FINAL ASSESSMENT
sections.text: WHAT DO WE KNOW? A real and significant series of cyber incidents affected refrigeration systems in Europe in October-November 2026. The 11-12 October France retail incident involved mass manipulation of refrigeration controller settings across roughly 700 sites, with product loss and at least 15 fires. Source ENISA confirmed a broader EU pattern and a second wave on 1-2 November 2026. Source France's national blood service experienced a provider-linked refrigeration control incident affecting three sites, but public reporting says stored blood products were not compromised. Source U.S. federal agencies publicly warned that malicious actors are targeting industrial refrigeration and cold-chain monitoring systems globally and identified key risk vectors. Source WHAT DO WE ASSESS? The dominant threat pattern involves remotely reachable refrigeration OT components with weak authentication, insecure configuration, and/or known vulnerabilities. The incidents demonstrate that refrigeration systems are now a practical sabotage target, not merely a theoretical ICS risk. The October France retail attack and the EFS incident are technically and operationally similar enough to merit joint defensive analysis, but not enough to claim one conclusively unified campaign. Public attribution is stronger for the October France retail incident than for the full set of November incidents. WHAT DO WE SUSPECT? Some incidents likely exploited exposed web administration interfaces or vendor / maintenance remote paths rather than deep enterprise compromise. Additional unreported or undisclosed refrigeration-system probing likely occurred outside the publicly confirmed victims. Commercial U.S. sectors that use similar refrigeration architectures may already have experienced scanning or attempted exploitation, even if public incident disclosures are limited. WHAT DON'T WE KNOW? The exact initial-access mechanism for each 2026 victim. The full set of affected countries, organizations, and controller models. Whether one actor or multiple actors drove the October and November waves. Whether the U.S. late-August commissary incidents were cyber-caused and, if so, whether they were technically related to Europe. The extent of any hidden physical equipment damage, insurance losses, or long-tail operational impact. WHAT EVIDENCE WOULD CHANGE THE ASSESSMENT? Public release of victim-side forensic reports, controller audit logs, or command history. Authoritative multi-country attribution or joint law-enforcement disclosure. Vendor-confirmed exploited CVEs tied to specific incidents. Pentagon / DeCA investigative findings on the August 2026 U.S. commissary outages. Country-specific CERT disclosures identifying shared infrastructure, credentials, or operator tradecraft across incidents. Overall judgment: The publicly available evidence supports a defensible conclusion that refrigeration and cold-chain OT systems have become an active target set for disruptive cyber operations, with demonstrated consequences for food safety, inventory loss, and potentially public health. Attribution beyond the October France retail attack remains limited and should be treated cautiously. Several high-value questions remain UNRESOLVED .
